1. Outside view. The base rate for Trump's "strongly approve" rating among registered voters in the Economist/YouGov poll has recently fluctuated between 17% and 22%. The series can move by 1 to 5 points between releases. A naive extrapolation from the most recent value (17.0%) would predict a similar value, perhaps with slight mean reversion towards 19-20%.

2. Inside view. We have search results for the latest Economist/YouGov poll released on Friday, November 13. The poll shows that among registered voters, 36% strongly or somewhat approve of Trump's job performance, which is tied with the previous week's post-election poll for his lowest approval rating. In the previous week's poll (fielded Nov 4-6), total approval among registered voters was also 36%, and the "strongly approve" component was 17%. Since the headline approval number for registered voters has remained exactly the same at 36%, the "strongly approve" component is highly likely to remain very close to 17%, likely falling between 16% and 18%. 

3. Pre-mortem. If this forecast is wrong, it is likely because the ratio of "strongly approve" to "somewhat approve" shifted despite the top-line approval number remaining flat at 36%. For instance, "strongly approve" could drop to 15% while "somewhat approve" rises to 21%, or vice versa. However, these internal components tend to be relatively stable week-over-week when the top-line number is unchanged. I will use a standard deviation wide enough to account for a 1-2 point internal shift.

4. Calibrate. A mean of 17.0% aligns perfectly with the previous week's internal breakdown for a 36% total approval rating. A standard deviation of 1.2 points will comfortably cover the 15.8% to 18.2% range, capturing the most likely variations in the strongly/somewhat approve ratio.
